title: The garden ledger
bodyMd:
Original literary narrative.

For three Saturdays I recorded every hour I spent in the community garden. I wanted the volunteer certificate for a school application, and the coordinator, Ben, signed my ledger without comment. I worked carefully, but when the clock struck noon I washed my hands and left, even if someone was still gathering tools.

On the fourth Saturday, Ben asked me to help Mrs. Imani move the seedlings from the cold frame. She read the labels aloud while I carried the trays. When I lifted one marked "beans," she stopped me. "That label is from last year. Look at the leaves." I looked, saw only green, and waited. She placed a second tray beside it. The leaves differed after all: one pair was broad and round, the other narrow as a pen nib.

We moved slowly. Mrs. Imani told me which seedlings had survived a late frost and which had been donated by a neighbor. By noon, I could distinguish three varieties without checking a label. I could also tell that one tray needed water. The coordinator passed with the tool cart, but I barely noticed.

When I finally reached the gate, Ben pointed to the ledger sticking out of my bag. I had forgotten to ask for his signature. He signed it, then handed me a spare set of gloves. "Next week?" he asked. I looked back at the seedlings, now small distinct populations instead of a blur of green. "Next week," I said.
